Someone called me a hungry boy for charging ₦200 to bring students together and teach them AI skills.

One thing I've noticed about Nigerians is how classist we can be. Even when someone makes an effort to make something valuable affordable and accessible to everyone, people still find a way to look down on it because of the price.

We've developed this mentality that anything valuable must be expensive. But price and value are two different things.

A cup of water costs almost nothing, yet it is one of the most valuable things you can have. A bottle of expensive wine can cost millions of naira, but that doesn't make it more valuable than water. The same applies to transportation and accommodation. You can meet basic needs affordably, but luxury comes at a premium.

I don't understand why people assume something must be expensive before it can be worthwhile.

In this case, we are not selling AI skills. We are bringing students together to learn how to use AI and other technologies to improve their studies and develop useful skills. The ₦200 fee is simply a screening fee to help ensure that participants are genuinely interested in taking the programme seriously.

Here's what we'll be learning at Book Cocaine:

- How to use AI to understand difficult concepts and lecture materials.
- How to analyse lecture slides and extract important information.
- How to turn lecture materials into MCQs and essay questions.
- How to use AI to practise for your actual examination format.
- How to build active-recall systems around your courses.
- How to create text-based and image-based flashcards.
- How to use Anki for repetitive learning and revision.
- How to study anatomy using illustrations, diagrams and AI-assisted explanations.
- How to build anatomical glossaries and organise unfamiliar terminologies.
- How to use AI for research, information retrieval and academic productivity.
- How to write effective prompts and get better results from AI tools.
- How to use AI to create images, videos and other digital content.
- How to use technology to work smarter and improve your productivity.
- How to develop useful soft skills and digital skills beyond your academics.

These are practical skills drawn from the things I have explored, learnt and shared on this account.

As a student in 2026, if you still don't understand how to use AI to improve your study methods, you are putting yourself at a serious disadvantage. The technology is already changing how people learn, work and solve problems.

I would rather make these skills accessible to students than package them at ridiculous prices simply to make them appear valuable.

PS5 14.10 KERNEL RESEARCH: #PF FAULT ORACLE DEFEATS DYNAMIC KASLR & RESOLVES 98 MB KERNEL IMAGE 🔓📍

Major exploit engineering release by @ZiggyVall and research team (Branch loader/fault-channel-and-descriptors / Probes 1001a–1005a):

• Dynamic KASLR Defeated on 14.10: Automated #PF (Page Fault) mapping oracle recovers the live kernel text base and per-boot KASLR slide in 33.5 seconds across retail hardware.

  • The #PF Discriminator: The loader’s signal handler receives the faulting context in RDX. Offset ctx+0x130 exposes the CPU page-fault error word: nibble 5 = Mapped Present (Supervisor kernel page) vs 4 = Unmapped.

  • Child Process Confinement: Scans run inside unprivileged thr_create(430) child threads (CS=0x43, SS=0x3B). When the child faults, the ROP chain dumps context and cleanly calls thr_exit(431). The parent process stays alive indefinitely with the same PID.

  • Kernel Text Boundaries Resolved Across Boots: 512-address sweep over retail hardware confirmed dynamic per-boot KASLR shifts:
  — Boot A Base: 0xFFFFFFFF91800000 (Slide: +0x11800000)
  — Boot B Base: 0xFFFFFFFFD8000000 (Slide: +0x46800000)
  — 98 MB (0x6200000) kernel text image mapped edge-to-edge, 2 MB aligned. No KPTI in process page table. https://t.co/raTW9q84gN

After Google acquired my AR startup, I started thinking about the next interface, this time for AI. Text and voice work fine, just like DOS did before the Mac. But nothing’s more intuitive than face to face.

After two years of research, today we’re launching Atmee v2: a real-time avatar model that makes live video agents feel truly life-like.

• Any character from 1 image + 10s of audio
• Contextual expressions, gestures, even interacting with the environment
• Live video calls, voice only, or video generation

At its core, Atmee v2 is a video foundation model, it can render anything, but it’s built to excel at characters, which is what video models like Seedance 2.5 and Wan 3.0 are mostly used for. In comparison:
Atmee v2

• Up to 50x faster
• 10-100x cheaper

Build tutors, sales coaches, support agents, companions, game characters, even whole living worlds. The interface after text and voice starts today.
